result.topic_en: Riemann converts a volume integral of the Laplacian of the potential into a surface integral and evaluates it over an infinitely small sphere, then works on the variational condition for aether displacements, rewriting the squared-derivative integral as a curl-type sum of squares plus a divergence term.
result.transcription:
Sieht man die Oberfläche $s$ und [-die darauf normal stehende die Normale darauf-] {+in jedem Punkte zugehörige Normale $p$+} auf der Fläche als Coordinaten an, so wird jener Ausdruck zu:

$\int\left(\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_3^2}\right)d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=\int\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_1}d\eta_2 d\eta_3+\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_2}d\eta_3 d\eta_1+\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_3}d\eta_1 d\eta_2\right)=\int\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}ds$

Für eine Kugel vom Halbmesser $r$ wird

$\int\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}ds=\int rr\frac{\partial V}{\partial r}d\Pi$

ist der Halbmesser unendlich klein, also

$[-r-]=dr$ und $\frac{\partial V}{\partial r}=\frac{V-V_0}{dr}$

wo $V_0$ der Werth des Potenzials im Mittelpunkt [-ist-] selbst, $V$ dagegen der {+in+} grosser Nähe des genannten Punktes ist, dadurch wird

$\int\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}ds=\int dr(V-V_0)d\Pi$

$=4\pi dr^2\cdot dr(V-V_0)$

In der allgemeinen Bedingungsgleichung ist außer $V$ auch noch $\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3$ zu bestimmen, wären diese {+nun+} [-auch-] schon daraus gefunden, so würde doch $\int\frac{\partial\eta_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}dt$ noch nicht bekannt sein, also muß man diesen Ausdruck als unbekannte Function [-$w=\int\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}dt$-] {+$\int\eta_i dt=w_i$+} ansehen, dadurch wird:

$0=\frac12\sum_{i,i'}\int\left\{\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial t}\right)^2+cc\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}\right)^2\right\}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3 dt+\int V\left(\sum\frac{\partial^2 w_i}{\partial\eta_i\partial t}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3+4\pi dm\right)dt+2\pi\int dm\sum\left(\frac{\partial\eta_i}{\partial t}\right)^2[?]dt$

Es ist $\int\sum_{i,i'}\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}\right)^2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=\int\sum_{i,i'}\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}-\frac{\partial w_{i'}}{\partial\eta_i}\right)^2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$ zu setzen

worin das erste 9 Quadrate, letzteres aber nur 3 enthält, denn die Ausdrücke:
$-2\int\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_2}\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_1}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=\div+2\int\frac{\partial^2 w_1}{\partial\eta_2\partial\eta_1}w_2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=-2\int\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_1}\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_2}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$

D. i. $-2\sum_{i\gtrless i'}\int\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}\cdot\frac{\partial w_{i'}}{\partial\eta_i}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$ geben mit $+\int\sum_i\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_i}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$ [?] die linke Seite

$\sum_{i\gtrless i'}\int\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_i}\frac{\partial w_{i'}}{\partial\eta_{i'}}d\eta$ [-$\frac{\partial w}{\partial\eta}\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial\eta_1}+\frac{\partial w}{\partial\eta_2}+\frac{\partial w}{\partial\eta_3}\right)\left(\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_1}+\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_2}+\frac{\partial w_3}{\partial\eta_3}\right)$ dieß für den leeren Raum $=0$-]
[-$\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_1}\left(\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_1}+\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_2}+\frac{\partial w_3}{\partial\eta_3}\right)$-]
$=\int\left(\sum\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_i}\right)^2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$ d. ist für den leeren Raum $=0$

methods.what: Divergence theorem: volume integral of Laplacian of V equals surface integral of normal derivative
methods.quote: $\int\left(\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_1^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_2^2}+\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial\eta_3^2}\right)d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=\int\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_1}d\eta_2 d\eta_3+\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_2}d\eta_3 d\eta_1+\frac{\partial V}{\partial\eta_3}d\eta_1 d\eta_2\right)=\int\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}ds$

methods.what: Flux through a sphere of radius r in spherical coordinates (solid angle element)
Evaluation of the flux over an infinitesimal sphere in terms of the deviation of V from its central value
Introduction of time-integrated displacement as a new unknown function
Variational (action) condition for aether motion with potential V and mass elements dm
methods.quote: $0=\frac12\sum_{i,i'}\int\left\{\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial t}\right)^2+cc\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_{i'}}\right)^2\right\}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3 dt+\int V\left(\sum\frac{\partial^2 w_i}{\partial\eta_i\partial t}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3+4\pi dm\right)dt+2\pi\int dm\sum\left(\frac{\partial\eta_i}{\partial t}\right)^2[?]dt$

methods.what: Rewriting the full gradient-squared integral as curl-type squares, using integration by parts to swap mixed derivatives
methods.quote: $-2\int\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_2}\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_1}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=\div+2\int\frac{\partial^2 w_1}{\partial\eta_2\partial\eta_1}w_2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3=-2\int\frac{\partial w_1}{\partial\eta_1}\frac{\partial w_2}{\partial\eta_2}d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$

methods.what: Divergence-squared term, vanishing in empty space
methods.quote: $=\int\left(\sum\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\eta_i}\right)^2 d\eta_1 d\eta_2 d\eta_3$ d. ist für den leeren Raum $=0$
